findings.detail: The `environment:` binding is removed from build-and-release, stage-release and publish-release. Previously production tags had to pass the environment's deployment protection rules before the Developer ID signing identity, the R2 keys and the coordinator release key (A-005) were released. Now `verify-source` in resolve-env is the only gate, and the new header comment says release jobs need no approvals and that the design assumes trusted repository writers. Any actor who can push a tag or dispatch a workflow from a branch, or who compromises a writer account, would no longer be stopped by a human approval step. The jobs hold the secrets that drive the binary-hash registry (A-011) and release registration. The old approval step was a second factor; the new check relies on one script on master and on the workflow file of the triggering ref. Fix: keep environment protection (required reviewers and branch/tag restrictions) on the credential-consuming jobs, or add an equivalent mandatory control outside the workflow, such as repository rulesets that protect tags and the workflow files. Also add this change to the threat model.
findings.title: Release jobs drop GitHub environment approval gates, leaving a source check as the only guard on signing and registry credentials

findings.detail: The summary text previously said the release key cannot approve builds, that qualification evidence goes to the admin app-attest builds endpoint, and that qualification stays an independent operator step. The head text now says the release endpoint validates and registers the exact official build before publication, and the job is renamed 'Register and publish exact signed release'. The qualification-request.json output is removed. The registration logic itself is not in this diff. If the CI release key's registration now creates or implies durable App Attest build qualification, T-054 and A-017 are weakened: a CI-key compromise or a malicious workflow run would be enough to make a build servable. Fix: confirm that release registration cannot create a durable qualification or approve a CDHash. Keep the qualification step separate and operator-authenticated. Update the threat model and the A-017/T-054 text to match the new flow.
findings.title: Publish flow now registers the signed build through the release endpoint, which may bypass the independent build-qualification step

findings.detail: The publish-release job registers the exact signed build with the coordinator using the env-scoped RELEASE_KEY, and the changelog and provider-trust.md state that per-release hardware qualification and manual approval are no longer required. The canonical model (A-017, T-054, TB-011 and the header notes) says an independently authenticated operator approves the exact binary and CodeDirectory, and that CI release keys cannot grant approval. A leaked PROD_RELEASE_KEY, or any repository writer who can run the workflow, can now register an arbitrary signed build. A build that passes only Apple signing then qualifies for protocol-3 serving. The remaining runtime checks (Apple proof, receipt, revocation) do not verify what the build does with plaintext prompts. Release jobs also no longer require environment approval (workflow header comment, lines 22-25). Fix: update A-005, A-017, T-054, T-024 and TB-011 to name CI and repository-writer compromise as an explicit trust dependency. Consider a re-introduced approval gate or protected environment for prod, a release key scoped to registration only, and alerting or a delay on new qualified hashes.
findings.title: CI release key now confers App Attest build qualification; threat model still says it cannot

findings.detail: In the publish-release job, the 'Install publication tools' step runs pip install awscli with no version or hash pinning, then prepends the venv bin directory to GITHUB_PATH. The next step runs provider-release-publication.py publish with RELEASE_KEY and the R2 credentials in its environment. A compromised awscli or transitive dependency, or a hijacked PyPI release, could read the production release key and R2 credentials. Because registration now implies serving qualification, this supply-chain path matters more than before. Fix: pin awscli with hashes, or use a vendored or preinstalled runner tool, and keep third-party tooling out of the process that carries the release key.
findings.title: Unpinned awscli installed from PyPI into the job that holds the release key

findings.detail: The base text of provider-trust.md invariant 4 says serving requires an approved artifact/code identity ("Build publication is not qualification"). The base canonical context says an independently authenticated operator approves the exact signed binary and full CodeDirectory, and that CI release keys cannot grant approval. The head text replaces this with "Trusted CI registers the complete official identity through the existing scoped release API". It also says that "CI and repository writers are trusted for official build identity" and that "per-release hardware qualification and manual approval are not required". A compromised CI pipeline or release key could therefore register a malicious build and obtain App Attest serving authorization, with no human approval and no physical-Mac check. The provider would then receive plaintext consumer prompts. The threat model still lists GitHub Actions/R2 as out of scope, and T-054, A-017 and TB-011 still assert approval independent of CI. The head text also says the platform persistence change must be deployed before the provider workflow is used. Running them out of order could register or reject builds inconsistently. Fix: update A-017, T-054, TB-011 and the scope list to cover the CI-to-release-API trust path and the missing approval gate. Add compensating controls such as a scoped, rotatable CI key, an audit log, rapid revocation, and an alert on new identities. Alternatively, keep the operator approval requirement.
findings.title: Docs drop the independent operator-approval gate for App Attest builds; threat model not updated

findings.detail: The build.md change says publication registers the exact official build through the existing scoped POST /v1/releases, and that "No per-release hardware qualification or manual approval is required". The base text instead gated publication on coordinator qualification. The canonical model (A-017, T-054, TB-011) says an independently authenticated operator approves the signed binary and full CodeDirectory, that CI release keys cannot grant approval, and that publication checks the approval under the revocation row lock. If the release key or a compromised release job now makes a build eligible for App Attest serving, a modified or revoked build could gain serving authorization (A-016) with no human gate. verification.md line 13 still asserts durable build qualification, so the docs contradict each other. Fix: keep the independent approval and revocation-lock check and make release registration unable to satisfy it. Otherwise update A-005, A-017 and T-054 to state the weaker trust root, and treat the release key as a qualification root.
findings.title: Release CI can now register builds as App Attest qualified, without independent operator approval

findings.detail: The new paragraph says secret-bearing release jobs accept signed annotated tags in reviewed master ancestry, or trusted master for dev/manual/recovery runs. It says they use repository-scoped secrets "without environment approval attachments" and "assume trusted repository writers". The base text, still unchanged at base line 320-322, says protected signing and publication jobs keep their existing approvals. A writer who can push to master, or trigger a manual or recovery run, can reach the signing and registration secrets without a second reviewer. Combined with the removed manual qualification step, that compromise yields a registered official build and the release API key (A-005), which feeds the release admission path (A-011) and App Attest build trust. The supply chain is out of scope, but the coordinator-side admission it now feeds is in scope. Fix: restore approval-gated environments for signing and registration, or update the threat model assumptions.
findings.title: Secret-bearing release jobs drop environment approvals and rely on trusted repository writers

findings.detail: docs/developer/build.md line 249 says release publication registers the exact official build through POST /v1/releases and that 'No per-release hardware qualification or manual approval is required'. Lines 251-255 add that secret-bearing release jobs use repository-scoped secrets without environment approval attachments and assume trusted repository writers. The canonical threat model (A-017, T-054) says an independently authenticated operator approves the exact signed binary and full CodeDirectory, and that CI release keys cannot grant approval. If this describes real behaviour, a compromised or abused CI release path or tag/master writer could mint App Attest serving-eligible builds without independent approval. That would weaken T-054 and A-017, and could let an unqualified or malicious provider build obtain serving authorization (T-052). If it does not, the doc misstates the trust model. The PR should either update T-054, A-017, A-011 and TB-011 to state what 'official build' registration authorizes versus App Attest qualification, or fix the text. It should also reconcile the 'no environment approval' statement at line 254 with line 327 ('retain their existing approvals'). I could not confirm the changed behaviour because only the file's head text was supplied.
findings.title: Docs describe official-build registration without per-release approval, conflicting with the threat model's independent build-qualification control
